copy.blurb:
The model fancies the draw more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Haiti. +4.2pp is a narrow gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the draw side.

On Elo, Brazil comes in 520 points ahead — Brazil at 1970, Haiti at 1450. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Brazil to win at 86%, the draw at 10%, and Haiti to win at 4%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. the draw on the win side reads 10%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Brazil to win at 92%, the draw at 6%, and Haiti to win at 3%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the the draw side — 6% on the market, 10% on the engine, a +4.2pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the the draw side that lower bound is 10% — +4.2pp clear of the market's 6%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the the draw side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 29 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +4.2pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

copy.summary: The model and the market disagree on whether a stalemate is in play here. Our prior puts the draw at 10%; Polymarket prices it at 6%. The +4.2pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Brazil v Haiti · the model leans the draw
